best_idea: Publish per-process counters through one coalesced write (at most one per second, with a trailing write for the last change) and probe peers with one in-flight check per id and a short timeout, so a dead zone process leaves the population sum without any blocking call.
decision_why: Keep coalesced writes, the trailing write, the per-id probe dedupe and the sweep guard; use a 300-500 ms probe timeout for a 20 Hz zone process instead of 2 s, and cache the global sum. Population counts are read-only for the engine, so they never decide a kill or a loot roll.
acceptance: A test runs a join burst of 500 clients in 1 s and asserts at most 2 counter writes in that second and a final write within 1 s of the last join; a second test stops one fake zone's ping and asserts its probe returns false within 500 ms and its count is gone from the total at the next 5 s sweep.
